sources.reason: BAHA Software Train game engine, levels, fonts and music with cc65 build. Source edition targets Atari 5200; broader Atari computer history does not establish every target builds here.

Line-anchored transcription and deterministic corrections produce EOS assembly. Only the first 8 KB bank is reconstructed; the second 8 KB is copied from a supplied reference ROM. Upstream matching/symbol reports are not independent validation.

Small cartridge bootstrap maps memory and installs the MICRO-INNOVATIONS IDE driver in RAM. The driver itself is deliberately absent; this repository is boot code, not a complete IDE-driver restoration.

Attributed mirror of scanned/transcribed IBM Technical Reference BIOS listings across PC, XT, AT and XT286 revisions. Toolchain and processor requirements vary by revision; not a universal 8086-compatible image.
Classic Macintosh slot-ROM dumping utilities and modern macOS parser. Parser explicitly models byte lanes and translated addresses; host-side processing is not a rebuilt Macintosh ROM.

Game, sound-engine and RAM-layout listings with semantic names for map, controller and score state alongside remaining numeric labels. Sparse README; no unsupported full-completeness or matching claim.

WLA-DX project targeting Japanese Rev 0 and USA/Europe Rev 1 with structured PSG command routines and symbol output. Distinct from SG-1000 Champion Tennis. Full matching is the stated aim, not independently tested.

In-progress commented Emulicious-derived listing with experimental modifications. Author warns commits can be unbuildable and output is not identical to original ROM; preserve uncertainty in comments.

Partial PAL-game exploration of size, graphics, menus and sound with annotated variables. Author explicitly disclaims full coverage and confidence in all interpretations; not a complete source restoration.
General CPU emulator, assembler, disassembler and debugger packages with source-map-aware console host. No machine peripherals implied; not a game-specific emulator.
Assembler, code formatter, language server and debug adapter. Inspected typed expression evaluator and source-map/codegen modules; compilation and editor integration not tested.
Standalone windowed debugger with instruction-delta reverse execution and VICE remote-monitor integration. CPU-only local emulation does not imply full computer hardware support.
Extension integrates assembly, launch, symbols and source-level debugging for Atari 8-bit projects. Source includes assembler command handling; bundled executables were not installed or run.
Native monitor with two-pass assembler, disassembler, tracer and memory utilities. Source uses .65s files and explicitly requires 65C02 instructions; conceptual portability is not 6502 compatibility.

Whole repository contains graphics/tutorial examples and attributed DefleMask/MML playback source. Selected player documents banked song data and channel state; not a new independently authored implementation of all components.

KOF95 ROM extractor documents renderer offsets, fragment lists and animation bytecode, plus Aseprite generation. Whole-character coverage is an upstream claim; do not classify it as reconstructed game logic.
Partial game-data library with pack, sprite, tile and level tools plus Lost Vikings VM disassembler/compiler. README explicitly says VM tools do not yet support Blackthorne.

Native Delphi/VCL rewrite of the Turbo Pascal DOS game by its original graphics artist, with BGI image decoding and double-buffer rendering. No whole-game behavioural equivalence independently established.

C reconstruction and x86 decoder for an EXEPACKed QuickBASIC game. Source documents SDL2/console modes and rounding/pixel-aspect adjustments. Repository explicitly describes AI-assisted work; completeness claims remain upstream.

Dedicated behavioural specifications and dated experimental findings accompanying acid-tetris-reborn. Documentation-only, not a second executable port. Sample determinism study retains contrary run outcomes instead of claiming perfect reproducibility.

Shared gameplay/resource C code with SDL2 native and WebAssembly hosts. Event source records evidence and corrected shared-tail handling; private IDA/research workspace is not distributed. Active RE, not a verified complete game.

Microsoft C/MASM reconstruction targeting 474.05 with explicit inferred-name/type boundary. Upstream reports exact output after a checked four-byte startup correction; no independent matching run. README explicitly credits OpenAI, Anthropic and Google LLMs without identifying model products.

Original author recovered source by disassembling a captured tape image in 2023; not surviving 1982 source. Header says disassembly incomplete and hardcoded tables can break modifications; copyright ownership remains uncertain in author's account.
DASM source for VIC-20 MIDI-interface cartridge with UART detection, baud configuration, keyboard and note lookup tables. Hardware availability and current firmware runtime not independently checked.

BBC Master puzzle demake with native rendering/game state, tile conversion and build scripts. Repository has little prose documentation; source and metadata establish scope, not complete compatibility.

Author re-created lost compiler/runtime work from scanned listings, adapting Tiny Pascal to CP/M. MBASIC compiler emits P-code with translator/runtime and examples; distinct rewrite/history explicitly retained.

Quill database conversion/listing tools and adventure sources, extending John Elliott's work for QL-specific 32-bit references and command differences. Future PAWS/DAAD goals not treated as implemented.

Reimplementation of Installer's LISP-like script language with MUI/Zune UI and relaxed resource limits. Source documents control forms against original guide; full V44.10 compatibility is a goal, not independently verified.

C/SDL2/OpenGL interpreter and graphics/audio modules informed by original AMOS source. Paula source explicitly approximates filtering. README overview and planned-feature list differ on browser support; no WASM target or cycle-accuracy claim promoted.

Early Kotlin decompiler with script blocks, variable models, opcode decoding and XOR-file tools, building on author's older Amiga work. Modern host tool; not an Amiga game port or complete SCUMM engine.

Raw OCR transcription visibly contains recognition corruption; author says considerable cleanup is needed. Retain as preservation/provenance material; reviewed EOS reconstruction is promoted separately without calling raw OCR assembleable source.

Upstream explicitly reports one callable service and 80 nonreturning stubs. Development probes are substantive, but do not promote this as a compatible replacement BIOS; revisit with implemented service coverage.
